To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
K/C, Cafestol and Turkish coffee increase hepatic Mgmt expression in a dose-dependent fashion.
K/C and Cafesto increase hepatic MGBT in a dose dependent manner up to a max of 2.5 fold at 0.125% K/C.

the coffee components Kahweol (K) and Cafestol(C), and their mixture (K/C), increase the activity of the DNA repair enzyme O(6)-Methylguanine-DNAmethyltransferase (MG MT) in rat liver in a dose-dependent fashion, whereas a lower increase was observed in rats treated with Turkish coffee.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of mechanisms by which coffee components may exert their anticarcinogenic activity.
the identification of a novel mechanism of chemoprevention by coffee components, namely the induction of DNA repair enzymes.
the potential of coffee to protect against colon cancer and the underlying molecular mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed increase in MGMT activity is a secondary effect, i.e. not the primary mechanism of the chemoprotective effects of coffee components.
the chemopreventative potential of coffee is based on a combination of several factors including the enhancement of DNA repair and detoxification.
the chemoprotective effects of K/C in animal models are mediated by both MGMT and GST-related enzymes, whereas the effects of Cafestol alone are mainly due to GST-related enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
K/C and Cafetol increase the expression of MGMT and GST-pi, and that the increase in the expression of MGBT is associated with the increase in GST-pi.
the chemopreventative potential of K/C in the liver may be based on a combination of enhanced DNA repair and enhanced detoxification.
the chemopreventative potential of coffee is not restricted to the modulation of xenobiotic metabolizing enzymes but that it also includes the induction of DNA repair.
The main takeaway from our work is that

K/C, Cafestol and Turkish coffee are capable of inducing MGMT in rat liver and that the magnitude of the effect is comparable to that of other known inducers of the enzyme such as phenobarbital, 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin and oltipraz.
K/C, Cafestol and Turkish coffee increase MGMT and GST-pi, and that the increase in GST-pi may be related to the increase in MGMT.
the chemopreventative potential of coffee is due to a complex mixture of compounds and not to any single component.
